title: Perf benchmarking sync - 2026-07-21
content:
Perf & Benchmarking Sync - 2026-07-21

Attendees:
- Asha Patel (owner)
- Miguel Santos
- Ryan Kim
- Li Wei
- Priya Nair

Agenda:
1) Quick status on weekly test runs
2) Investigate latency & throughput regressions seen after kernel-selector change (PR#432)
3) Plan follow-up experiments and rollbacks if needed
4) Blockers / help needed

Summary / context:
- We observed a regression in tail latency and a small throughput drop after merging kernel-selector change in PR#432 (merged 2026-07-18). The change alters kernel selection heuristics for fused-attention for sequences > 128.
- Regression surface appears on A100 and some T4 clusters for batched workloads. No impact observed on CPU-backed inference.

Recent test runs (full harness: nightly-bench + synthetic chat workloads):
- Test harness: bench-v2 (continuous-bench), config: batch sizes [1,4,8,16], seq lengths [32,128,512], model: redwood-7b-v1, quant: q4_0
- Primary regression: p99 latency (seq=32, batch=8) increased from ~210ms -> ~370ms (+76%). p95 increased from 120ms -> 180ms.
- Throughput: tokens/sec for chat-static workload decreased ~8% for batch sizes >=8 on A100. Small batches (1,4) unaffected.
- KV-cache long-context runs (seq=512) show ~10% higher memory churn leading to GC spikes on some nodes (observed in SRE traces).
- Regression not reproducible on dedicated-nightly small cluster (different kernel build); seems tied to runtime kernel-selection logic and a fallback path introduced in PR#432.

Hypotheses / likely root causes:
- Kernel selector heuristic incorrectly chooses generic CUDA kernels for certain batch/seq combos post-change, causing slower execution path.
- Fallback path for fused-attention when a specialized kernel is not found has a cold path cost (kernel compile/caching) that spikes p99 for first few requests per instance.
- Interaction with our quantization path (q4_0) + fused kernels might force additional data layout conversions, increasing per-token overhead for larger batches.
- Memory churn from KV-cache evictions is amplifying GC pauses for long-context tests (seq=512) - possibly unrelated but worsens tail latency on heavy workloads.

Logs / evidence reviewed:
- Bench traces: gs://redwood-bench/runs/2026-07-21-14-30 (bench-v2) - see p95/p99 comparisons and per-kernel time breakdown.
- SRE traces: traces.redwood/internal/trace-2026-07-21 (GC spikes on node gpu-a100-12)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/432 - kernel-selector change set and CI logs
- Jira: INF-9876 contains customer-reported regression and reproducibility notes

Immediate action items (owners + ETA):
- Asha: run targeted microbench to isolate kernel selection for batch=8, seq=32 across kernel builds (baseline before PR#432, after PR, and with forced selection). Due: 2026-07-22
- Miguel: add verbose kernel-selection logging behind feature flag to runtime to capture which kernel IDs are chosen and when fallback happens. Deploy to canary pool. Due: 2026-07-22
- Ryan: reproduce the compile/cold-start hypothesis by running cold-start heavyweight bench (restart instance between runs) and measure p99 over warmup. Due: 2026-07-23
- Li: investigate KV-cache eviction heuristics and memory churn for seq=512 tests; propose short-term tweak to eviction threshold. Due: 2026-07-24
- Priya: evaluate rolling back PR#432 on a small canary cluster to compare end-to-end perf and customer impact. Coordinate with SRE. Due: 2026-07-22

Short notes from the canary run (2026-07-21 14:30):
- Canary with verbose logging showed that for batch=8 seq=32 some instances select generic-kernel-v2 instead of fused-attn-optimized-v1. Instances that hit generic kernel show high per-token time.
- Observed ~3 cold-compiles in the canary window - those correlate tightly with p99 spikes.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Do NOT hotfix production immediately; prefer targeted canary experiments and a rollback option if canary confirms regressions at scale.
- Prioritize logging/observability so we can confidently track which kernel is used for affected customer requests.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Is the generic kernel slower only for certain model graph shapes? (action: Asha to test variant models)
- Should we add a small randomized warmup on new instance startup to avoid first-request cold-compile spikes? (action: Ryan to prototype)
- How to safely force kernel preference per-deployment (feature flag + override)? (action: Miguel)

Blockers / help needed:
- Need SRE help to provision a protected canary cluster with recent runtime build + verbose logging. (SRE: @infra-oncall)
- PR access: if rollback is decided, need release-engineering support for quick revert/rollout.

Next sync:
- Weekly perf sync: 2026-07-28 10:00 PT. Quick check-in on 2026-07-22 after initial canary results.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep an eye on customer INF-9876 - potential SLA impact if not resolved.
- Add unit test harness to simulate kernel-mismatch path to catch future regressions in CI.

Attachments / links referenced in meeting (paste into Jira/Confluence):
- bench run: gs://redwood-bench/runs/2026-07-21-14-30
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/432
